rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 2 'Scan your history for the work that recurs': line 26: bolded blockquote lead '**Cut the scan when the top patterns are clear enough to use.**' -- 12 words, an entire sentence, not a <=5-word handle (the rule's own line: 'Bold the handle (<=5 words, a sub-span), never a whole lead sentence.'). chunk 3 'Draw your top work-shapes as diagrams': line 41: bolded blockquote lead '**Want to see the shapes, not read them?**' -- 8-word question, same defect. Harm: this is the exact pre-2026-07-09 whole-sentence-bold pattern the rule exists to kill, just relocated onto a blockquote lead instead of a bullet lead; it crowds the true handle signal ('Fast operator?' on L24, 2 words, is a correctly-scoped handle in the same file, showing the intended shape). The maintainer's L71 note ('bold only on widget/label chrome and blockquote callout leads') states the file's general bold-placement policy but does not address the word-count cap on these two specific leads, so it does not read as a dated accept-note excusing this instance the way the sibling module file's L relevant note explicitly does for its own two short (<=5-word) blockquote leads.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Trim both bolded spans to a short handle and leave the rest of the sentence plain -- e.g. bold only 'Cut the scan' and 'Want to see the shapes', matching 'Fast operator?''s already-compliant shape.
